items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: He said, 'He is the drummer that I hired. I told him that he had the job.' ... 'Get Lee Young for me'.

ctx.x: Freddie Fisher was his name. It came out in the DownBeat, May 1, 1943 in big red letters across the top of it, in bold type, it says "Color loses Lee Young's job" -- then it goes on to tell you, you know, what transpired, but I think one of the reasons a thing like that could happen at the time was because of the separation of the locals.

I think earlier I had told you that the white local, they worked 6 days a week, you know, and that the black local, they worked 7 days a week; that's when I was coming up and I would let drummers get off and I'd work in their place for free -- well, what happened with this, there was a rule in Los Angeles that any transfer musician that came in to L.A. -- and I think that was a national rule, too; it may have been a
